text: The vectors $$ \wvec_1 = \fourvec1111,\hspace{24pt} \wvec_2 = \fourvec11{-1}{-1},\hspace{24pt} \wvec_3 = \fourvec1{-1}1{-1} $$ form an orthogonal set of 4-dimensional vectors. Since there are only three vectors, this set does not form a basis for $\real^4$. It does, however, form a basis for a 3-dimensional subspace $W$ of $\real^4$.
